title: indigo_agent_scheduler: reject @enabled with @priority hook and test the rejected hook level in the integration suite
description:
Follow-up of 0baf77fb (commit c90c4ceee), requested by the owner.
- @enabled has no effect on a task of the hook priority class (a hook start never checks it). Add it to the keys rejected with @priority hook (HOOK_REJECTED_KEYS in indigo_drivers/agent_scheduler/indigo_agent_scheduler_header.c), with the same 'line N: @enabled: not allowed with @priority hook' error, in either order. Verify first in indigo_agent_scheduler.c that ENABLE/DISABLE task commands and is_enabled() do not rely on a hook-class task carrying @enabled; if a DISABLE command on a hook-class task rewrites the header with @enabled, make that command rejected for hook-class tasks or otherwise keep the stored text valid, and say so in a note.
- Add an integration case in indigo_test/integration/test_agent_scheduler.c: uploading a task with '@priority hook 50' through AGENT_SCHEDULER_ADD_TASK is rejected (property Alert, no task stored, message names the line), and one for @enabled with @priority hook.
- Update the unit test for @enabled, the guide (INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md) and doc/SCHEDULER.md lists of rejected keys, and increment the scheduler agent DRIVER_VERSION.

outcome.summary: Reviewed diff master...HEAD (d1c20e399). Header: HOOK_REJECTED_KEYS now includes KEY_ENABLED (indigo_agent_scheduler_header.c:59); conflict reporting at :586/:607-608 uses max(conflict_line, priority_line), so both orders report 'line 3: @enabled: not allowed with @priority hook'; unit test covers both orders and removes @enabled from the accepted-keys case. Claim verified: TASK_COMMAND ENABLE/DISABLE only set task->disabled (indigo_agent_scheduler.c:2627-2630), persisted as disabled=N in the status line (:604, :641-642); is_enabled() = header.enabled && !disabled (:395); no code writes @enabled into task text, so no stored hook task can become unloadable via the agent. Integration case hook_priority_class_rejects_a_level_and_scheduling_keys requires INDIGO_ALERT_STATE via change_text, checks the line-2 @priority and line-3 @enabled messages and task_count()==0; it is registered and PASSed in the command-1 log (116 run, 116 passed). Docs: guide line 221 and SCHEDULER.md line 175 list @enabled. DRIVER_VERSION 0x03000015 -> 0x03000016. whitespace, unit and command-1 recorded at HEAD d1c20e399 (tree 9b8bad657b, matches current tree). No defects. Coverage limits: I did not rerun the builds or tests; I relied on the recorded check logs.

history.text: Edits done; running unit check then scheduler integration
Check command-1 started: make -j8 -C indigo_drivers/agent_scripting -f ../../Makefile.drv all && make -C indigo_test test-agent-scheduler

Decisions: HOOK_REJECTED_KEYS gains KEY_ENABLED (same 'line N: @enabled: not allowed with @priority hook' error, either order). ENABLE/DISABLE task commands only toggle the separate in-memory/status flag task->disabled (persisted as disabled=N in the status line, never written into the header text), and is_enabled() = header.enabled && !disabled; hook starts never call is_enabled (is_hook checked first), so a hook-class task never needs @enabled and no stored task text can acquire @enabled through a command. No code change to the commands was needed. Residual: pre-existing stored hook text that carries @enabled would now fail to parse on load, same trade as the previous ticket's other keys. Mapping: unit hook_priority_rejects_scheduling_keys (@enabled both orders; hook_priority_class no longer lists @enabled as accepted); integration hook_priority_class_rejects_a_level_and_scheduling_keys ('@priority hook 50' -> Alert, line 2 message; '@enabled no' with hook -> Alert, line 3 message; no task stored). Docs: INDIGO_SCHEDULER_GUIDE.md, doc/SCHEDULER.md. DRIVER_VERSION 0x03000015 -> 0x03000016. Checks: whitespace+unit passed (header unit suite 15 cases pass); scheduler integration via 'make -C indigo_test test-agent-scheduler': 116 run, 116 passed, 0 failed.
